metric_rationale: Calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic (choosing the option with more feature-wise wins). By design, the experimental trials pit the Tallying heuristic's deterministic preference against the Flipped-Majority prediction. The Tallying theory will score highly on this metric (near 1.0, minus noise), whereas the Advocated Flipped-Majority theory will score very poorly (near 0.0, plus noise).

This metric isolates the trials where the two theories make strictly opposite deterministic predictions. Specifically, it filters for trials where one option has more positive features than the other (Trials 1 and 2). Tallying strongly prefers the option with more positive features, while the Anti-majority ensemble (dominated by the flipped majority aligning with Take The Best) strongly prefers the option with fewer features but the single highest validity cue. The metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with Tallying on these critical trials, yielding a value near 1.0 for the Advocated Theory and near 0.0 for the Competing Theory.

Across all trials in the design, one option always has more 1s (4 ones) while the other has fewer 1s (3 ones). The Advocated Theory (Anti-majority ensemble) consistently predicts the option with more 1s, because that option loses under TTB and WADD (which prioritize the high-validity features where it has 0s) but wins under Tallying, causing a majority vote against it that the model then flips. Conversely, the Competing Theory (Anti-Tallying) explicitly treats 0 as better than 1 and tallies these 'anti-wins', so it systematically prefers the option with more 0s (and thus fewer 1s). This metric simply calculates the proportion of trials where the subject chose the option with more 1s, expecting ~1.0 for the Advocated Theory and ~0.0 for the Competing Theory.

The experimental design pits Anti-Tallying against Anti-Majority by constructing trials where the majority of standard heuristics (TTB and WADD) agree on one option, while Tallying prefers the other. Anti-Majority flips the majority choice, effectively aligning with Tallying. Anti-Tallying, by treating 0s as wins, acts as the exact opposite of Tallying. Therefore, the two models predict completely opposite choices on every single trial. This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the Anti-Tallying prediction, yielding a value near 1 for Anti-Tallying and near 0 for Anti-Majority.

In the chosen experimental design, the majority of the three standard heuristics (TTB, Tallying, WADD) always favors the option that is superior on the most valid feature (feature 1). The Competing Theory (Soft TTB) will thus consistently favor the option with a 1 on feature 1. The Advocated Theory (Anti-majority), by definition, will consistently flip this preference and favor the option with a 0 on feature 1. This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's chosen option has a 1 on the highest-validity feature. The Competing Theory expects this value to be high (>0.5), while the Advocated Theory expects it to be low (<0.5), resulting in a maximal and highly stable contrast.

By design, all trials in this experiment are constructed such that the three standard heuristics (TTB, Tallying, WADD) agree on the preferred option. Soft TTB will consistently lean toward this majority-preferred option (which is the TTB option), whereas the Anti-majority model deterministically flips the majority decision and leans toward the exact opposite. Measuring the proportion of choices that align with the TTB prediction will yield a value > 0.5 for Soft TTB and < 0.5 for the Anti-majority model, providing a massive, highly robust discrimination gap.

By design, the Advocated Theory (Anti-majority) consistently prefers the option with exactly 3 positive ratings, whereas the Competing Theory (Reverse WADD) consistently prefers the option with exactly 4 positive ratings across all trials. Measuring the proportion of choices where the selected option has a sum of 3 perfectly discriminates between the two models' deterministic predictions.

In the experimental design, Reverse WADD systematically prefers the option that has a 1 on the most valid feature (feature index 0) across all trials, because it tries to minimize the overall WADD score and the competing options are constructed such that the one with a 0 on the first feature has a much higher sum of validities on the remaining features. In contrast, the Anti-majority model frequently votes against the option with a 1 on the first feature, because TTB and Tallying often form a majority that favors it, causing the contrarian ensemble to flip its choice to the option with a 0 on the first feature. Measuring the proportion of trials where the chosen option has a 1 on the first feature yields ~1.0 for Reverse WADD and ~0.25 for Anti-majority, strongly discriminating the two theories.

In the chosen experimental design, the Advocated Theory (Anti-majority ensemble) perfectly aligns with the Take The Best (TTB) choice because Tallying and WADD consistently agree against TTB, forming the majority that the model then flips. Conversely, the Competing Theory (Anti-TTB) deterministically predicts the exact opposite of the TTB choice. By simply calculating the proportion of trials where the subject's response matches the TTB choice (driven by the highest validity cue, which is always the first feature here), we can maximally dissociate the two theories. The Advocated Theory will produce a value close to 1 (minus noise), while the Competing Theory will produce a value close to 0 (plus noise).

The experimental design constructs trials where the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic is always in the minority against Tallying and WADD. As a result, the Competing Theory (Anti-majority) will always invert the majority and end up predicting the TTB choice. The Advocated Theory (Anti-TTB) deterministically predicts the opposite of TTB. Therefore, measuring the proportion of trials where the subject chooses the option opposite to TTB perfectly discriminates the two theories: it will be high for Anti-TTB and low for Anti-majority.
